title:
Structural Biology
Computational Agent
chapter: Methods, Research Landscape and System Architecture
lead: A research and implementation proposal for an extensible scientific agent
take: Author: Yi Zhou
notes: English edition of the 30-slide research presentation. Capability maps describe target scope, not completed deployment or measured performance.

title: Research Roadmap
lead: Establish the field and research question before introducing architecture and experiments
body: 03–12: methods, nine systems, research gaps and hypotheses
13–16: capability maps, system design and control loop
17–26: specifications, planning, tools, state, validation and deployment
27–30: controls, ablations, safety and development gates
take: Goal: an extensible scientific execution system, with tools and validators as units of capability.

title: Structural Research Connects Multiple Modalities
lead: Sequences, experiments and models contribute different forms of scientific evidence
take: Shared requirement: preserve object identity, parameters, artifacts and interpretation across tools.
notes: Prediction, experimentally restrained modeling, search and mechanistic analysis support different claims. A predicted model does not by itself establish experimental support, object identity or causality. This page organizes inputs and task roles without ranking methods across unrelated benchmarks.

title: Agent Foundations: Reasoning, Action, Observation
lead: A model proposes decisions, tools return observations, and a runtime constrains permitted actions
body: Form candidate plans and decision summaries
Execute tools and observe actual results
Update actions under permission, budget and stopping rules
take: Feedback informs decisions. Gains on question-answering or interactive tasks require scientific validation.
notes: Original ReAct author diagram: reason-only, act-only and combined reasoning/action. This is a methods illustration, not a structural-biology experiment from this project. Audit actions, observations and decision summaries without requiring disclosure of private model reasoning.

title: Agent Methods Change Different System Components
lead: Compare mechanisms and assumptions rather than treating papers as a single performance ranking
body: Observe after acting. Incorrect observations can still mislead.
Dependency DAG and ready calls. Parallelism obeys real constraints.
Reuse verbal feedback without necessarily updating weights. Verify it.
Tree search and evaluation need reliable feedback and extra budget.
Optimize LM programs on development data. Freeze final tests.
Coordinate models, people and tools. Consensus is not ground truth.
take: Combine mechanisms according to task feedback, action cost and evaluation reliability.
notes: Original evaluations cover QA, code, web and interactive environments. They do not establish performance on this project’s scientific tasks. DSPy is an offline optimization method, not a mandatory online tool-loop stage. Reflexion can reuse verbal experience without updating model weights. Distinguish the AutoGen paper’s mechanism from later SDK versions.

title: Workflow, Single Agent or Multiple Agents?
lead: Fixed computation can use explicit paths. Dynamic selection and collaboration need measurable benefits
body: Reproducible paths and low control cost. Define branches in advance.
Observations can change the next step
One state and budget. Define tool semantics and stopping rules.
Explicit roles add communication, duplicate work and coordination risk.
take: Implementation options: LangChain / LangGraph, Google ADK and AutoGen. Evaluate state and recovery needs.
notes: Conceptual patterns, not a quantitative ranking. Report success, cost, latency, errors and human intervention under matched tools and budgets. Frameworks do not map one-to-one to patterns. LangChain organizes models, tools and middleware. LangGraph supports stateful workflows and agents. ADK provides agent and workflow components. Framework features do not ensure scientific correctness. Start this project with one controller and a persistent state graph; test collaboration as an additional mechanism.

title: A Research-Role Map of Biological Agents
lead: Nine examples occupy different research roles: frameworks, research systems and software entry points
take: Compare knowledge access, tool execution, feedback and the evidence supporting each conclusion.
notes: A representative, overlapping classification rather than an exhaustive map or common autonomy ranking. BioChatter is an application framework. Biomni and CellAgent are research systems. Phenix and CryoNet entries use official implementation or capability documentation, which is not comparable to a shared benchmark protocol.

title: Knowledge, Analysis and Experimental Decisions
lead: These routes change different stages of research and use different kinds of feedback
body:
Knowledge graphs, RAG and model/API chains.
Integration needs external fact-checking.

Retrieve tools/data, plan and execute code.
Public cases do not cover every structural task.

Plan, execute and evaluate with tool retrieval.
Single-cell evidence depends on data and metrics.

Select the next round from perturbation feedback.
Data-based evaluation, not wet-lab automation.
take: Knowledge, execution and experiment-selection mechanisms still need domain-specific quality criteria.
notes: Left: BioChatter author-manuscript Fig. 1, snapshot 2024-02-23, preserving its original meaning. The other three systems do not share this diagram. CellAgent follows the 2024 preprint mechanism, without mixing later-version scores. BioDiscoveryAgent illustrates experimental selection, not an instrument-control protocol.

title: Structural Agents: Software and Quality Gates
lead: Scientific engines build, fit and refine models. Agents organize steps, constraints and review
body:
LLM analysis and planning
Parameter allowlists, stage gates

Bounded by software and data
Final structures need expert review

Typed input catalogue
Shared session and job entry

An interface is not a blind test
Accept individual tools separately

Reasoning with local execution
Expert approval for major edits

Evidence supports bounded tasks
Not universal autonomous solving
take: Professional tools, domain rules and human checkpoints belong in the execution path.
notes: Phenix documents PERCEIVE, THINK, PLAN, BUILD, VALIDATE and OUTPUT; LLMs mainly participate in THINK and PLAN. CryoNet descriptions use the archived official HTML when live retrieval timed out. StructAgent here is Xiaohu Guo’s cryo-EM system, not the unrelated arXiv:2607.11388 namesake. Cases and product documentation cannot support direct success-rate comparisons.

title: Protein Engineering: Design and Hypothesis Tests
lead: Generation, prediction, simulation and experimental validation support different levels of evidence
body:
Group chat coordinates planning and critique.
Tools combine generation, prediction and physics.

Computational design and physics examples.
Compare collaboration at matched budgets.

Generator–reflection pairs organize research.
Code and analysis retain or revise hypotheses.

Computational studies of protein properties.
Limited by sampling, models and conditions.
take: Generated scores, independent calculations and experiments provide different kinds of evidence.
notes: Left: original ProtAgents Fig. 1, preserving its meaning, not our architecture. ProtAgents demonstrates computational studies rather than a universal scientific benchmark. Sparks combines generation, prediction, secondary-structure/property models and MD. Surrogate scores or simulations do not establish experimental confirmation. External validation remains necessary.

title: From Existing Systems to Our Research Questions
lead: Existing work closes several research loops. Reliability across broader task combinations still needs testing
body: Keep chains, residues, coordinates, units, composition and sampling conditions consistent across tools.
Control branching and recovery when inputs are incomplete, tools fail, candidates fail or long jobs stop.
Check files, execution and scientific conclusions separately, with traceable supporting evidence.
Test across objects, tasks and tool combinations using matched budgets, external scoring and injected faults.
take: These are empirical research questions. Untested differences between systems are not research findings.

title: Positioning and Testable Hypotheses
lead: Study an extensible structural-biology agent for task organization and reliable scientific execution
body: Make objects, goals, conditions and acceptance rules explicit
Test reductions in identity errors and cross-tool inconsistency
Combine tool semantics, persistent state and bounded replanning
Test completion and recovery cost on new task combinations
Use independent validation and bind report claims to artifacts
Test reductions in invalid artifacts and unsupported conclusions
take: Broad capability is the goal. Establish actual availability with adapters and reference tests.
notes: These hypotheses and benefits remain to be tested. Start with one controller, extensible tools and validation rules. More agents, a model upgrade or a larger compute budget do not automatically establish improved scientific validity.

title: Capability Map I: Data, Building and Experiments
lead: Organize tasks by modality across proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, glycans and complexes
body: Search sequences, structures or local density; expand hits
Inspect, segment, localize, build and refine maps
Coordinate transforms, local quality, map–model support
NMR, SAXS, XL-MS and multimodal restraints
take: These are target task families. Executable scope depends on tool integration, inputs and reference tests.

title: Capability Map II: Analysis, Simulation and Design
lead: Analysis modules can run independently or form new research workflows through the agent
body: Quality tables, mappings, transforms, comparison definitions
Interfaces, contacts, channels, ligands, nucleic acids, membranes
Units and limits of geometry, energies and scores
Protein/ligand docking, subunit placement, symmetry, clashes
Candidate poses, sampling and independent rescoring
Trajectory processing, clustering, free energies, transitions
Sampling, convergence, errors and physical conditions
Stability/binding changes, sequence and structure design
Candidates, controls, failure risks and experimental tests
Coarse graining, networks, allostery, multimodal visualization
Model assumptions, evidence and scope of mechanisms
take: A capability adds a task contract, scientific tool, validator and reference tests.

title: Structural Biology Agent: Core Architecture
lead: Separate model cognition, deterministic control, scientific execution and evidence management
body: Task specifications, capability/knowledge retrieval, context assembly, LLM planning and revision
Plan compilation, type checks, state machine, budgets and recovery
Permission gateway, job scheduling, scientific tools and real artifacts
Tool contracts, state/artifact references, independent quality checks and report support
Validated results, methods, limitations and human review
take: Models propose plans and explanations. Runtimes enforce permissions. Validators inspect actual artifacts.
notes: Proposed system architecture, not a linear workflow. Research tasks and data enter through specification. A context builder combines retrieved capabilities and recorded observations for the planner. Actions pass deterministic plan checks, a permission gateway and job management. Independent validation writes structured observations into evidence/state for later decisions. Tool documentation, checkpoints and immutable artifacts remain logically separate. The legend distinguishes control, assets/state and feedback.

title: The Agent Loop: State, Actions and Validation
lead: Explicit state supports action selection, controlled execution and the next state update
body:
Specs, observations, asset refs
Allowed tools and budget

Choose a structured action
or revise a local plan

Types, rights, preconditions
Budget and stopping rules

Sync tools / async jobs
Attempts and artifacts

Results and errors
Independent validation summary

Plan nodes and artifacts
Checkpoints and actual usage
take: Persist actions, observations and decision summaries. Internal reasoning is not computational evidence.
notes: A plan is a candidate execution scheme, not a scientific fact. The policy may revise a local plan using observations. Changed scientific intent requires a new specification version. Runtime and scientific checks are external constraints: a model cannot turn failure into success through explanation. Stop on exhausted budgets or unrecoverable failures.

title: Task Specifications Make Intent Computable
lead: Example request: compare two complex interfaces and identify which contacts change
body: Two models, target chain pairs, residue correspondence, ligand and atom selection
Compare contact counts, contact composition, geometry or energy changes?
Alignment strategy, distance threshold, units, missing residues and alternate conformers
Auditable mappings and contact tables; change lists, views and limitations
take: Clarify missing conditions. Version specification changes instead of silently changing the question.
notes: This illustrates task understanding and specification, not JSON that an existing endpoint necessarily accepts. Other tasks need modality-specific fields: map voxel/origin/axis, trajectory topology/periodicity/time units, or reflection data with working and validation sets.

title: Planning Combines Retrieval and Dependencies
lead: Retrieve applicable capabilities, then compose steps with compatible input and output conditions
body: Filter tools by semantics, input types, preconditions, versions and resources
Build a dependency DAG and identify the artifact passed on every edge
Check available inputs, type compatibility, resources and required validation
Use observations to adjust candidates or local steps within revision and total-cost limits
take: Treat plans as hypotheses for execution. Run tool actions only after the relevant checks.

title: The Registry Makes Scientific Tools Discoverable
lead: A tool contract describes semantics, execution conditions and verifiable artifacts
body: Required information from the tool adapter
Supported questions, unsupported claims, valid data and method assumptions
Structured schemas, asset refs, coordinates/units, types and postconditions
Container, software/weights/database versions, CPU/GPU, licenses, services
Error classes, timeouts, idempotency keys, checkpoints and retry conditions
Companion validator; registration, environment health and reference-test status
take: Admit a tool to planning only after its adapter and reference tests pass.

title: State Controls the Next Action
lead: The model reads recorded facts. An external state machine enforces actions and stopping rules
take: Recoverable failures permit bounded revision. Store scientific quality separately from job status.
notes: Record action requests, observations and decision summaries. State handles waiting, recovery and termination. Language cannot override failed validation. Account for all attempts when enforcing budgets.

title: Long Jobs Are Independent of Model Sessions
lead: Use one job interface for small synchronous tools, asynchronous CPU/GPU work and remote computation
body: Bind frozen specifications, parameters, permissions and resource budgets

Run small tools directly
Queue long tasks
Allocate workers
job_id, heartbeat, progress, logs, actual usage and cancellation
Input/output hashes, tool versions, attempts and a complete artifact manifest
take: Resume from persistent state after network loss. Idempotent submission prevents duplicate expensive jobs.

title: Context, State, Knowledge and Artifacts
lead: Give the model sufficient decision context while keeping scientific data in controlled storage
body: Current goal, observation summaries, candidate actions and asset IDs
Spec versions, plan nodes, past attempts, budgets and questions awaiting confirmation
Tool documentation, methods, validated workflows and applicability conditions
Raw files, models/maps/trajectories, logs, metrics and transform chains
take: Memory provides reusable experience. Current artifacts provide evidence. Check versions and applicability.

title: Validation Separates Execution from Science
lead: One agent framework uses different scientific validators according to the task specification
body:
Files, schema, provenance
Objects, parameters, run records

Structures: mapping, geometry
Maps: coordinates, density support
Trajectories: sampling, convergence

Claims cite real artifacts
Verify numbers and objects

Accept / reject / insufficient
Keep unresolved limits
take: Exit code 0 usually means software-defined success. Scientific results still require independent validation.

title: Example I: Unknown Density to Candidate Models
lead: With only a density region, the system selects branches according to available inputs
body: Confirm map region, coordinates, candidate scope and required evidence
Search map-first, or build a backbone before structural retrieval

Check fit, density and geometry.
Flag insufficient evidence.

Rank candidates with evidence.
Link views and follow-up tasks.
take: Reuse the architecture with replaceable tools. A top retrieval score alone cannot establish protein identity.
notes: Illustrative proposed workflow. The figure is an official CryoNet.Discovery example, not a run of this project’s agent.

title: Example II: Motion and Interfaces in Trajectories
lead: Question: how do domain motion and interfacial contacts change together during this simulation?
body: Topology/trajectory, time units, periodic boundaries, chains/regions and analysis definitions
Unwrap and align; run geometry, contacts and clustering as dependencies permit
Check atom mappings, sampling windows, correlation, convergence and uncertainty
Time series, representative conformations, statistics and limits of physical interpretation
take: Trajectory adapters and validators reuse the control design. Correlated changes do not establish causality.
notes: Proposed scenario, not a completed MD analysis. Parallel branches must share preprocessing versions and time indices. Mark limited evidence when sampling is inadequate; trajectory frames are not independent samples.

title: Deployment: Services, Workers and Evidence
lead: Separate cognition, job execution and scientific data, coordinating them through persistent state
body: Web workbench and task/asset models, e.g. FastAPI/Pydantic
A state graph such as LangGraph, model adapters and retrieval
Queue, leases, idempotency, cancellation and events
CPU/GPU/HPC workers, object storage, metadata and independent validation
take: Fix module contracts and pass real reference tasks before enabling dynamic model-driven composition.
notes: Recommended design. Web/API and agent services do not directly execute arbitrary scientific commands. The job service invokes isolated workers. A relational database stores tasks, state, versions and permissions. Object storage holds models, maps, trajectories and logs. Registries and validators are versioned separately. The first release need not implement every GPU/HPC backend.

title: Experiments Measure the Agent’s Contribution
lead: Hold tools and data capabilities fixed while comparing decision and control mechanisms
body:
Execute a preset plan
as a stable task baseline

Same model, tools, budget
Choose steps dynamically

Add task constraints,
quality gates and bounded revision

Use one frozen scorer
and retain all tasks in denominators
take: Report task success, scientific errors, abstention quality, total cost and elapsed time without assumed gains.

title: Optimization Starts with Failure Attribution
lead: Held-out combinations and mechanism ablations test generalization as well as cost
body: Hold out families, objects or task combinations. Freeze databases and preprocessing; track contamination.
Remove task contracts, runtime validation feedback and recovery policies separately.
Missing fields, wrong mappings, incomplete artifacts, timeouts, unavailable tools and malicious content.
Separate intent, planning, tool, data, validation and explanation errors. Regress after changes.
take: Use tasks or families as statistical units, with paired comparisons and intervals. Attempts are not independent.

title: Safety Controls Are Part of Execution
lead: A model must respect the tool gateway, data policies and resource boundaries
body: Tool allowlists, parameter/path checks, isolation, quotas and idempotent submission
Project isolation, private-structure egress policies, restricted import of untrusted PKL/directories
Bind expensive computation, sensitive egress and scientific-spec changes to concrete approvals
Tracing, alerts, recovery, backups, rollback and reproducibility bundles
take: Release gates combine safety tests with scientific regression tests, enforced outside the model.

title: Development Roadmap and Delivery Gates
lead: Progress by verifiable system capabilities while expanding scientific task coverage
body: Task families, asset model, tool/validator schemas, reference tasks
Defined inputs/outputs and an independent scorer
Fixed workflows, adapters, persistent jobs and artifacts
Model planning, observations, bounded revision, evidence delivery
Budget-matched controls, ablations and fault tests
More tasks, GPU/HPC adapters and operational support
Reference-task and operational acceptance per capability
take: One agent architecture, an expanding scientific tool ecosystem, and independently auditable delivery.
notes: Implementation roadmap for the 30-slide proposal. Existing PRD 0.2 remains the defined development baseline. Extend contracts and adapters for new scientific tasks rather than creating a parallel baseline. This update delivers research/design material, not a newly deployed agent service.
